r16float_mid.rule_note: H2 TEST (hypothesis-to-falsify). Literal = 0.5 - 2^-25 = exact fp32 0x3EFFFFFF, not representable in fp16, 2.98e-8 below 0.5 and 2.44e-4 above the next fp16 value down (0x37FF = 0.499755859375, in the adjacent lower exponent bracket). Registered expectation 0x3800 (round-to-nearest-even: the true value is far closer to 0.5 than to 0x37FF, so RNE must cross the exponent boundary upward). H2 alternative (candidate, from EXP-0075's single uncorroborated observation, NOT promoted here): store-path narrowing truncates the source mantissa toward zero without ever crossing the exponent boundary, giving 0x37FF. This is the case that separates RNE from truncation; see r16float_pos_trunc for the symmetric positive-direction probe.

r16float_pos_trunc.rule_note: NEW (EXP-0079): positive-direction truncation-direction probe, H2 companion to r16float_mid. Literal = 0.5 + 2^-12 exactly (exact fp32 0x3F001000), which is the EXACT halfway point between fp16 0x3800 (0.5) and fp16 0x3801 (0.50048828125) in the SAME exponent bracket as 0x3800 -- no boundary crossing is at stake here. Both round-to-nearest-even (0x3800 is the even-mantissa neighbour) and round-toward-zero truncation (drops the exact-half remainder, i.e. floors) predict 0x3800, so this point does not by itself separate RNE from truncation. It DOES separate 'round-toward-zero' from a 'round-away-from-zero/ceiling' alternative, which would predict 0x3801: combined with r16float_mid (which shows the store path stays BELOW 0.5 rather than crossing up to it), an observed 0x3801 here would refute simple toward-zero truncation and reopen the question; an observed 0x3800 corroborates toward-zero truncation as the unique rule consistent with both probes.

r16float_third.rule_note: fp32 constant fold 0x3EAAAAAB converts to fp16 0x3555 (0.333251953125) under RNE (corroborated for RGBA16Float on this host by EXP-0070); RNE and truncation coincide at this point (not diagnostic for H2 by itself).

r16sint_1.rule_note: typed int store path; read fills (r,0,0,1) with alpha 1 (fill behavior corroborated for R32Uint on this host by EXP-0070).

r32float_exact.rule_note: CORRECTED (EXP-0075 registration slip, disclosed in its RESULTS.md and its PRE_REGISTRATION.md re-derivation check): exact fp32 passthrough of 0.5 is 0x3F000000, texel LE 0000003f -- NOT 0x3F800000/0000803f (that was 1.0, and was an arithmetic slip in the EXP-0072/EXP-0075 chain, independently confirmed wrong by EXP-0075's own hardware observation of 0000003f, which is internally consistent with its own read-word expectation 3f000000). No format-conversion hypothesis is being tested here: fp32 texture, fp32 input, direct passthrough, no rounding.

r32float_third.rule_note: fp32 round-to-nearest-even of 1/3 from the compiler constant fold.

r8snorm_m100.rule_note: H1 TEST (hypothesis-to-falsify, not an established fact): registered expectation 0x80 is the [-1,1]->[-128,127] asymmetric-clamp public convention (Metal/D3D-family documented snorm decode uses value/127 with -128 clamped to -1.0, but the ENCODE side has two competing public conventions). H1 (candidate, from EXP-0075's single uncorroborated run and NOT promoted here) predicts 0x81 instead: encode = round(c x 127) as a symmetric scale, giving round(-127) = -127 = 0x81. Typed read decodes to -1.0 under EITHER byte (both clamp to -1.0 on read), so the physical texel byte is the only discriminator; this run's observation falsifies or corroborates H1, it does not merely repeat it.

r8snorm_p050.rule_note: tie under x127 scale: 0.5*127 = 63.5; expected 64 under round-half-even/half-up, 63 under truncation. Exact 64 under x128 scale (no tie). Read decodes 64/127 = 0x3F010204.

r8snorm_p100.rule_note: +1.0 -> 127 under both candidate encode scales (x127 rounded; x128 clamped).

r8unorm_p050.rule_note: tie: 0.5*255 = 127.5, floor(x)=127 odd/floor+1=128 even. Expected 128 under round-half-even AND round-half-up (they coincide at this tie because 127 is odd); 127 under truncation. This point alone cannot separate half-even from half-up (see r8unorm_sep_a/r8unorm_sep_b, which use an even-floor tie to do that). Read decodes 128/255 = 0x3F008081 (corroborated for RGBA8Unorm on this host by EXP-0070).

r8unorm_p100.rule_note: unorm8 encode: clamp to [0,1] then scale by 255; 1.0 -> 255; typed read fills (r,0,0,1).

r8unorm_sep_a.rule_note: NEW (EXP-0079): half-even vs half-up separator, non-discriminating control point. 1.5/255 is a tie between floor=1 (odd) and 1+1=2 (even): round-half-even picks 2 (the even neighbour) and round-half-up ALSO picks 2 (it always rounds n.5 up), so this point cannot separate the two rules by itself -- it exists to confirm the harness/format produce a clean tie response before r8unorm_sep_b is interpreted. Expected 0x02 under both round-half-even and round-half-up; 0x01 under truncation. Confounder: the literal 1.5/255.0 is evaluated at compile time in fp32, so the encoder-side product c*255 may differ from the mathematical 1.5 by a few ULP of fp32 double-rounding (~1e-7 relative); this is far smaller than the 1-part-in-255 tie width and is not expected to move the case across the tie, but is recorded as an alternative not excluded.

r8unorm_sep_b.rule_note: NEW (EXP-0079): half-even vs half-up DISCRIMINATING separator. 2.5/255 is a tie between floor=2 (even) and 3 (odd): round-half-even picks 2 (stays at the even neighbour, i.e. rounds DOWN); round-half-up picks 3 (always rounds n.5 up). Expected 0x02 (round-half-even hypothesis, registered per the r8unorm_p050 precedent); the falsifying alternative is 0x03 (round-half-up). 0x01 under truncation (a third, already-disfavoured candidate). Same fp32 double-rounding confounder as r8unorm_sep_a, noted there.

rg11b10float_exact.rule_note: CORRECTED (EXP-0075 registration slip, disclosed in its RESULTS.md and predicted in advance by its own PRE_REGISTRATION.md re-derivation check, then hardware-confirmed by EXP-0075's single run): layout is R in bits[10:0] (e5m6, no sign), G in bits[21:11] (e5m6), B in bits[31:22] (e5m5), independently re-derived and verified here by a from-scratch bitwise fp32->eXmM converter (bias 15, round-to-nearest-even mantissa truncation with carry). fp11(0.5)=0x380, fp10(0.5)=0x1C0, word = 0x380 | 0x380<<11 | 0x1C0<<22 = 0x701C0380, texel LE 80031c70 -- NOT the EXP-0072-inherited 0038c071 (word 0x71C03800), which does not decode to (0.5,0.5,0.5) under this layout and was never independently re-derived before EXP-0072/EXP-0075 adopted it verbatim. Authored alpha ignored (format has no alpha).

rg11b10float_mid.rule_note: H2 TEST, corrected layout (see rg11b10float_exact). Under round-to-nearest-even, an independently-coded fp32->eXmM converter confirms R=G=fp11(mid)=0x380 and B=fp10(mid)=0x1C0 -- identical to the exact-0.5 word 0x701C0380/80031c70, because the 11-/10-bit mantissa rounding of this literal crosses the same boundary as fp16 does. Registered expectation is therefore 0x701C0380/80031c70 (RNE). H2 alternative (candidate, from EXP-0075's single uncorroborated observation, NOT promoted here): toward-zero truncation with NO exponent-boundary carry gives R=G=0x37F (E=13,M=63), B=0x1BF (E=13,M=31), word 0x6FDBFB7F, texel LE 7ffbdb6f -- independently recomputed here from the corrected layout and matching EXP-0075's raw observation bit for bit, which is itself evidence the corrected layout is right, not evidence H2 is right. Read words under the H2 alternative would be 3efe0000 3efe0000 3efc0000 (0.49609375/0.49609375/0.4921875) instead of the registered 3f000000 x3.

rg16float_exact_mid.rule_note: R is exact fp16 0.5 (rule a, no uncertainty). G carries the SAME H2 uncertainty as r16float_mid: registered expectation 0x3800 (RNE), H2 alternative 0x37FF (truncation) for the G halfword only. Layout: R halfword 0, G halfword 1.

rg8snorm_m100_zero.rule_note: H1 TEST: carries the -1.0 encode-scale question of r8snorm_m100 in the R channel (G is exact 0.0, no uncertainty). Registered expectation 0x8000 (R=0x80); H1 alternative 0x8100 (R=0x81).

rg8snorm_p100_p050.rule_note: per-channel snorm8; carries both the +1.0 and 0.5-tie uncertainties of r8snorm_p100/r8snorm_p050 (round-half-even/half-up tie, not the H1 scale question).

rg8unorm_p100_p050.rule_note: per-channel unorm8 as in r8unorm_p100/r8unorm_p050; layout R byte 0, G byte 1.

rgb9e5float_exact.rule_note: exactly representable: channel = M * 2^(E-24) with 9-bit M, shared 5-bit E; canonical MSB-set normalization gives M=256, E=15; word = R | G<<9 | B<<18 | E<<27 = 0x7C020100, texel LE 0001027c. Authored alpha ignored. Unchanged from EXP-0075 (already independently re-derived and hardware-confirmed there).

rgb9e5float_mid.rule_note: H2 TEST. At shared exponent E=14 the true mantissa value is 511.99999998..., which under round-to-nearest overflows the 9-bit field to 512 and canonically renormalizes to E=15, M=256 -- the exact-0.5 word 0x7C020100/0001027c (registered expectation). H2 alternative (candidate, from EXP-0075's single uncorroborated observation, NOT promoted here): the mantissa is truncated toward zero with NO overflow renormalization, giving E=14, M=511 in all three channels, word 0x77FFFFFF, texel LE ffffff77, read words 3eff8000 x3 (0.4990234375) instead of the registered 3f000000 x3. Public specs do not pin the overflow-renormalization behavior; this remains explicitly uncertain either way.

rgba16uint_pack.rule_note: four channels in one texel; little-endian halfword order R,G,B,A; alpha authored 0 (real channel, no fill).

rgba8snorm_pack.rule_note: H1 TEST: four distinct channels exercising all snorm8 sub-cases at once (R carries the H1 -1.0 scale question, B carries the round-half-even/half-up 0.5 tie, G and A are exact). Registered expectation 0x8000407f (R=0x80); H1 alternative 0x8100407f (R=0x81), everything else unchanged.
